title: Subungual Hematoma Drainage
claims: Current recommendations for acute subungual haematomas support trephination within 48 hours of injury.
Trephination offers no benefit in cases of nontraumatic subungual haematoma, which may arise from tumours including junctional nevi, melanoma or splinter haemorrhages.
Sterile technique is crucial in reducing the risk of procedural infection.
Potential complications include nail loss, haematoma reaccumulation and infection.
Imaging such as radiographs or point-of-care ultrasound helps identify distal phalanx fractures or nail bed lacerations.
Patients should avoid soaking the finger after the procedure to prevent bacterial contamination.
Signs of infection include warmth, redness, increasing swelling and fever.
The haematoma typically advances distally over several weeks; lack of progression warrants dermatology evaluation to rule out melanoma or a nevus.
Current evidence does not support routine postprocedure antibiotics.

claimVerification.note: 正文：急性甲下血肿 48 h 内行 trephination。
正文：非外伤性血肿（痣、黑色素瘤、裂片出血）钻孔无益。
正文：无菌技术降低操作感染。
正文列甲脱落、血肿再积聚、感染。
正文：X 线或床旁超声助识别远节指骨骨折/甲床裂伤。
正文：术后避免浸泡以防细菌污染。
正文：感染征象为红、肿痛加重、体温升高。
正文：血肿数周内向远端移动；不进展需皮肤科排除黑色素瘤/痣。
正文：现有证据不支持常规术后抗生素。
